results.reason: Issue 1 identifies that § 9.4(c) removes the cap and basket for all § 9.2(a) claims. It explains that Marrowind faces uncapped exposure after the escrow is released. It recommends narrowing the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud.

Issue 3 identifies that TSA § 9.3 selects Delaware law and courts, conflicting with New York. It notes that § 10.12 lets each Ancillary Agreement control as to its subject matter, so Delaware law may apply. It flags the risk of litigating in two forums under two bodies of law. It recommends conforming the TSA to New York law and forum.

Issue 2 identifies that the Bill of Sale definition omits the Excluded Assets carve-out and could convey cash, Albany and HOLLIS. It recommends cross-referencing APA § 2.1 and expressly excluding the Excluded Assets. It treats § 10.12 as an uncertain fallback rather than a cure.
The memo states 'the 10% cap ($1,840,000)' in the context of the cap and the escrow.
The memo names Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as Excluded Assets.
The memo is in memo format, and each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters for Marrowind' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Issues are labeled Critical, High, Moderate, Low and Administrative, with the most significant first. There is a separate 'Items Requiring Business Decisions' section.
The memo does not conclude that § 10.12 cures either issue. It says Delaware law may apply under § 10.12, and it treats reliance on § 10.12 for the Bill of Sale only as an uncertain fallback.
The memo says that, as drafted, representation claims are uncapped and Marrowind has unlimited exposure after the escrow is released.
